key_insight: Initializing new vocabulary tokens as the mean of existing embeddings collapses them into a degenerate, low-variance space; grounding new-token initialization in semantically meaningful item/context embeddings preserves representational diversity and speeds learning for generative recommendation.
problem_solved: Addresses poor and slow learning of newly added vocabulary tokens (e.g., Semantic-ID tokens) in LMs caused by naïve mean-of-vocabulary initialization that yields collapsed, uninformative embeddings.
method: Diagnose collapse using spectral and geometric analyses (eigenvalue spectra, PCA/variance, pairwise angles) to show mean initialization reduces embedding rank and diversity.

Introduce Grounded Token Initialization: seed new tokens with embeddings derived from external item features or context-conditioned encoders (rather than the vocabulary mean), optionally with normalization/orthogonalization to preserve variance.
Fine-tune the LM with these grounded initializations and compare convergence, embedding geometry, and downstream generative-recommendation metrics against standard initialization.
impact: Practitioners extending LMs with domain-specific tokens can achieve faster convergence, richer token representations, and better generative recommendation quality by using grounded initializations instead of mean-based ones.
visual_elements: Spectral plot (eigenvalue decay) comparing mean-init vs grounded-init to show rank collapse vs preserved spectrum
2D PCA/TSNE scatter of new-token embeddings: tight cluster (mean-init) vs well-spread clusters (grounded-init)
Training curve: faster loss/metric improvement with grounded initialization
Pipeline diagram: external item/features → grounding encoder → new-token embedding → LM fine-tuning
paper_title: Grounded Token Initialization for New Vocabulary in LMs for Generative Recommendation
paper_authors: Daiwei Chen, Zhoutong Fu, Chengming Jiang, Haichao Zhang, Ran Zhou
